title: Root-level CorrelationMatrix/EfficientFrontier/RiskDecomposition are dead duplicate code
description: `components/CorrelationMatrix.tsx`, `components/EfficientFrontier.tsx`, `components/RiskDecomposition.tsx` are byte-for-byte identical to `components/portfolio/CorrelationMatrix.tsx` etc. (confirmed via `diff`). Only the `portfolio/` versions are imported (from `PortfolioChart.tsx:14-16`). Root-level copies are dead code bundled into the vendor chunk increasing build output.
recommendation: Delete `src/components/CorrelationMatrix.tsx`, `src/components/EfficientFrontier.tsx`, `src/components/RiskDecomposition.tsx`. Run `npm run build:typecheck` to confirm no broken imports.
acceptance_test_hint: `vite build` completes with no import errors; bundle size decreases by ~3 deduplicated chunks

title: PortfolioMetrics interface missing analytics fields — escaped with `as any`
description: `PortfolioMetrics` interface does not declare `correlationMatrix`, `efficientFrontier`, or `diversificationScore`. `PortfolioChart.tsx:102` uses `(metrics as any)?.correlationMatrix`, line 110 `(metrics as any)?.efficientFrontier?.points`, line 112 `(metrics as any)?.efficientFrontier?.optimalPosition`. `Portfolio.tsx:443` uses `(metrics as any)?.diversificationScore`. These `as any` casts silently hide schema drift if the backend changes field names.
recommendation: Extend `PortfolioMetrics` in `portfolioSlice.ts` with optional typed fields: `correlationMatrix?: Record<string, number>; efficientFrontier?: { points: {risk: number; return: number}[]; currentPosition: {risk: number; return: number}; optimalPosition?: {risk: number; return: number} }; diversificationScore?: number`. Remove all `as any` casts.
acceptance_test_hint: `tsc --noEmit` passes with no errors in Portfolio.tsx and PortfolioChart.tsx

title: Three dead production dependencies: `react-beautiful-dnd`, `plotly.js`, `react-plotly.js`
description: `grep -rn "react-beautiful-dnd" src` — 0 results. `grep -rn "from 'plotly" src` — 0 results. `grep -rn "from 'react-plotly" src` — 0 results. Yet `package.json` lists all three as production `dependencies`. Plotly alone is ~2.8MB minified; it inflates `npm install` time and may be included in vendor chunks if the manualChunks guard is encountered unexpectedly.
recommendation: Remove `react-beautiful-dnd`, `@types/react-beautiful-dnd`, `plotly.js`, `react-plotly.js`, `@types/react-plotly.js` from package.json. Run `npm install` then `npm run build` to verify no broken imports.
acceptance_test_hint: `npm run build` completes; `du -sh dist/assets/plotly*` returns no files

title: Catch-block uses `err: any` and leaks raw API error detail to UI
description: `InvestmentThesis.tsx:169` — `catch (err: any) { setError(err.response?.data?.detail \
acceptance_test_hint: 'Failed…') }`. Displaying `err.response?.data?.detail` verbatim can leak internal server error messages, stack traces, or database field names to the user. This is an XSS-adjacent pattern if the backend ever returns user-controlled content in `detail`. | Replace `err: any` with `err: unknown`. Use a typed error handler: `const message = isAxiosError(err) && err.response?.status !== 500 ? err.response?.data?.detail : 'An error occurred'`. Never display 500-level detail to users. | Unit test: mock a 500 response with `detail: 'SQL error: ...'` and assert the displayed message is the generic fallback string

title: WebSocket subscribes to `state.portfolio.watchlist?.items` — property path not in PortfolioState
description: `websocket.service.ts:144` — `state.portfolio.watchlist?.items`. Looking at `portfolioSlice.ts`, the state structure contains `watchlists: Watchlist[]` and `selectedWatchlist: Watchlist
recommendation: null` but no `.watchlist.items` direct path. This access silently returns `undefined`, so watchlist stock subscriptions are never sent to the server — no real-time price updates for watchlisted items.
acceptance_test_hint: Fix the state access to match the actual Redux state shape: `state.portfolio.selectedWatchlist?.items \ | \ | []` or iterate `state.portfolio.watchlists`. Add an integration test for `subscribeToChannels`. | Manual test: add a stock to watchlist, observe WebSocket `subscribe` emit in browser DevTools Network

title: `stock:trade` event handler delegates to unimplemented `handleTradeUpdate`
description: `websocket.service.ts:81-84` — `this.socket.on('stock:trade', (data) => { this.handleTradeUpdate(data); })`. No `handleTradeUpdate` method is defined in the class. TypeScript strict mode does not catch this because it appears to be callable but `this.handleTradeUpdate` will throw `TypeError: this.handleTradeUpdate is not a function` at runtime on every trade event.
recommendation: Implement `handleTradeUpdate(data: unknown): void` or replace with an inline dispatch. Add a `TradeUpdate` interface.
acceptance_test_hint: `websocket.service.ts` compiles without error; unit test: mock socket, emit `stock:trade`, verify no TypeError

title: Route prefetch `setTimeout` leaks memory if component unmounts before timeout fires
description: `App.tsx:96-103` — `const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => { routesToPrefetch.forEach(prefetchRoute); }, 1000); return () => clearTimeout(timeoutId)`. The cleanup is correct. However `prefetchRoute` calls `routeModules[route]()` which triggers a dynamic import — if the import resolves after the component has unmounted, React will log a state update on unmounted component warning. The imported modules are side-effect free so this is low risk, but the pattern is not idiomatic.
recommendation: The existing `clearTimeout` cleanup is correct. No urgent fix needed. Consider replacing with `requestIdleCallback` for non-essential prefetching to avoid competing with visible page resources.
acceptance_test_hint: No "Can't perform state update on unmounted component" warnings in console after rapid navigation

title: No test coverage for `api.service.ts`, `websocket.service.ts`, or `api.config.ts` — core integration layer
description: `find src -name "*.test.*"` — no test file for `services/api.service.ts`, `services/websocket.service.ts`, `config/api.config.ts`. These files implement the auth interceptor, token refresh, WebSocket reconnection — the most business-critical client logic. With the schema mismatches found (F-12-001, F-12-002), tests would have caught these issues.
recommendation: Add vitest unit tests for: (1) `api.service.ts` interceptor behavior (401→refresh→retry); (2) `websocket.service.ts` connection/reconnect lifecycle; (3) `api.config.ts` URL construction helpers.
acceptance_test_hint: `npm run test:coverage` shows api.service.ts and websocket.service.ts at >80% branch coverage

title: Service worker file registered and exported but never called — dead runtime code
description: `serviceWorkerRegistration.ts` exports `register()` and `unregister()`. `index.tsx` imports `reportWebVitals` but does NOT import or call `serviceWorkerRegistration.register()`. The file is never invoked; no service worker is active. The prior audit noted "Missing PWA service worker registration" as a gap.
recommendation: Either remove the file if PWA is not a goal, or call `register()` in `index.tsx` after deciding on a caching strategy. Leaving the unreferenced file is misleading.
acceptance_test_hint: If removed: `npm run build:typecheck` passes. If activated: Lighthouse PWA score improves.

title: No RTK Query — all data fetching uses hand-rolled thunks without request deduplication or cache
description: `store/slices/dashboardSlice.ts`, `portfolioSlice.ts`, `marketSlice.ts` all use `createAsyncThunk` for data fetching with manual loading/error state. No cache TTL, no deduplication, no automatic refetch on focus. With 40+ endpoints, the boilerplate volume is high and inconsistent (some slices have `isLoading`, others use `status`).
recommendation: Evaluate migrating to RTK Query for server state; keep slice reducers only for client/UI state. This would eliminate ~60% of thunk boilerplate and add automatic caching, deduplication, and refetch.
acceptance_test_hint: RTK Query baseApi established; at least 2 feature APIs migrated; bundle size neutral or better

title: `state.sortBy = action.payload.sortBy as any` — type escape in reducer
description: `recommendationsSlice.ts:163` — `state.sortBy = action.payload.sortBy as any`. This cast bypasses Immer's draft type checking and allows any value to be assigned to `sortBy`.
recommendation: Define a `SortBy` union type and type the payload properly: `action: PayloadAction<{ sortBy: SortBy }>`. Remove `as any`.
acceptance_test_hint: `tsc --noEmit` passes without `as any` in recommendationsSlice

title: Design doc in `src/design/` belongs in `docs/` not in the source tree
description: `src/design/PORTFOLIO_DASHBOARD_DESIGN.md` is a Markdown design document inside the TypeScript source directory. It will be included in `tsc` file indexing and may confuse documentation tools.
recommendation: Move to `docs/design/PORTFOLIO_DASHBOARD_DESIGN.md` or delete if superseded.
acceptance_test_hint: `find src -name "*.md"` returns no results

title: No `React.memo` on any page-level component — all pages re-render on any store change
description: `grep -rn "React.memo\
recommendation: export default memo" src/pages/` — 0 results. Pages re-render whenever any Redux state changes because they are not wrapped in `memo()`. Layout component triggers all child page renders on sidebar toggle, search open, or notification add.
acceptance_test_hint: Wrap page components in `memo()` where `props` are stable. Identify selectors in pages that pull large slices (e.g. `state.portfolio`) and use `createSelector` memoized selectors. | React DevTools profiler shows page components do not re-render on sidebar toggle

title: `recentSearches` persisted to localStorage without TTL or size limit
description: `SearchModal:67` — `localStorage.getItem('recentSearches')`, `SearchModal:105` — `localStorage.setItem('recentSearches', JSON.stringify(updated))`. No max age, no cap on number of entries (no limit on the `updated` array). Over time this can grow large.
recommendation: Add a max of 10 entries (slice to 10 before storing) and optionally a `savedAt` timestamp to expire old entries after 30 days.
acceptance_test_hint: Unit test: add 15 searches; assert stored array length is ≤ 10

title: `target: runtime` references missing stage in Dockerfile.backend
description: Production compose builds with `dockerfile: ./Dockerfile.backend` and `target: runtime`, but root Dockerfile.backend has only unnamed builder/runtime stages (`as builder` at line 9, no `AS runtime`). Build fails with "target stage runtime could not be found".
recommendation: Either rename root Dockerfile.backend stages to include `AS runtime` (and `AS development`, `AS test` referenced by dev/test compose), or change `dockerfile:` to `./infrastructure/docker/backend/Dockerfile.optimized`.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.production.yml build backend` succeeds

title: Dev compose `target: development` not defined in root Dockerfile.backend
description: Root Dockerfile.backend has no `AS development` stage. dev/test compose overlays will fail builds for the same reason as F-13-001.
recommendation: Add named stages to root Dockerfile.backend or repoint compose to `infrastructure/docker/backend/Dockerfile.optimized` which defines `AS development` and `AS runtime`.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml build` succeeds

title: Test compose `target: test` does not exist anywhere
description: No `Dockerfile.backend` (root or infrastructure variant) defines an `AS test` stage. Test runs cannot start.
recommendation: Add `AS test` stage with pytest deps, or reuse `runtime` and override CMD only.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.test.yml up --abort-on-container-exit backend` exits 0

title: CNAME records point to placeholder + invalid target type
description: DNS CNAME content set to `your-server-ip.com` for api/www/static. CNAME requires a hostname — if literal IP intended, must be `A` record. All `yourdomain.com` strings are placeholders. File is not deployable.
recommendation: Replace with real domain via env templating (e.g., Terraform `var.domain`); switch to A records for IPs; remove/parameterize the file.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -E 'yourdomain | your-server-ip' infrastructure/cdn/cloudflare_config.yaml` returns 0

title: Source bind-mounts in base compose leak into production
description: Base `docker-compose.yml` (which `production.yml` extends) mounts `./backend:/app/backend` and `./frontend/web:/app`. The production overlay does not declare `volumes: []` reset, so production containers run host source code instead of the immutable image — defeats reproducibility, breaks read-only filesystems, complicates rollback.
recommendation: In docker-compose.production.yml, explicitly set `volumes:` for backend/frontend services to only the runtime mounts (logs, models:ro, data) and either remove dev mounts from base compose or split bases so prod doesn't inherit them.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.production.yml config | grep -A3 'backend:' | grep -q './backend:/app/backend'` returns nothing

title: nginx prod healthcheck hits `/nginx_status` only allowed from internal IPs
description: Healthcheck `curl -f http://localhost/nginx_status` runs inside the container; localhost matches `allow 127.0.0.1` so it works at runtime. But `/nginx_status` is only defined inside the **HTTP** server block in nginx.optimized.conf:282-290 — the **HTTPS** server (line 93) does not define it. If the healthcheck is bound to 443 only (TLS), it will return 404. Conflict with `/health` endpoint that IS defined on both servers (lines 180,275).
recommendation: Change healthcheck to `curl -f http://localhost/health` for parity with infrastructure/docker/nginx/nginx.conf:55 and nginx-ssl.conf:113.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -fs http://localhost/health` inside container returns 200

title: `ssl_dhparam` and `ssl_trusted_certificate` reference files not in repo
description: nginx-ssl.conf requires `/etc/nginx/ssl/dhparam.pem` and `/etc/nginx/ssl/chain.pem`. `ssl/` directory contains only `.gitkeep`. Production startup will fail with `cannot load certificate "/etc/nginx/ssl/dhparam.pem"`.
recommendation: Generate dhparam at deploy time (compose init container or Makefile target) and document that chain.pem must come from Let's Encrypt; OR remove `ssl_dhparam` and `ssl_trusted_certificate` directives if not strictly required.
acceptance_test_hint: `nginx -t` inside investment_nginx_prod returns "test is successful" with provisioned certs

title: TA-Lib downloaded via insecure `http://prdownloads.sourceforge.net`
description: Plain HTTP download; redirect chain susceptible to MITM, breaks reproducibility. infrastructure/docker/backend/Dockerfile uses `https://github.com/ta-lib/ta-lib/releases/...` — preferred.
recommendation: Use the GitHub URL; pin to a specific tag/sha; verify checksum.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n 'http://prdownloads' Dockerfile.backend` returns 0 hits

title: Embedded heredoc Python downloads FinBERT inline at build
description: Inline `python -c "..."` block downloads `yiyanghkust/finbert-tone` during image build. Network during build is fragile, ties build to HuggingFace availability, increases image size by ~500MB+. Also references `backend/ml/models/` for `COPY` — directory may not exist (broken_dependency in some checkouts).
recommendation: Move model download to runtime init container or to ML scope's model registry. Verify `backend/ml/models/` exists or remove the COPY.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker build -f infrastructure/docker/backend/Dockerfile.optimized .` succeeds offline-only after model is cached out-of-band

title: Embedded `RUN echo 'server {...}'` overwrites the prior COPY of nginx.conf
description: Lines 45-46 COPY `nginx.conf` and `security-headers.conf`, then lines 49-66 echo a literal default.conf that overrides defaults — dual-config pattern is fragile and config drift between embedded server block and the COPYed conf is high.
recommendation: Drop the inline echo; rely solely on the COPYed configs. Keep one source of truth.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker run <frontend> cat /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` shows no embedded `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;` if removed

title: Duplicate HTTP and HTTPS server blocks with full app routing
description: Both port 80 and 443 server blocks define `location /`, `/api/`, `/ws`, etc. Port 80 should only do ACME + redirect (per nginx-ssl.conf which does this correctly). Current optimized.conf serves the app over plain HTTP.
recommendation: Reduce HTTP server to ACME challenge + 301 redirect to HTTPS; remove duplicated app routes from port 80.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -sI http://host/` returns `HTTP/1.1 301` Location: https

title: `location` blocks inside an included security-headers file
description: nginx `include` of a file containing `location {}` directives is only valid when included inside a server block. The same file is included in nginx.optimized.conf:115 *inside* server{}, fine, but in nginx-ssl.conf:110 also inside server{} — works. However the conf-mode duplication (security-headers.conf in nginx/conf.d auto-loaded vs security-headers.conf in frontend/) creates two divergent files. The frontend variant has location blocks; the nginx variant does not. This means `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` is enforced on the frontend SPA — will break embedded third-party widgets unless explicitly opted in.
recommendation: Consolidate into one canonical security-headers.conf. Reconsider COEP=require-corp for SPA — typically `unsafe-none` or `credentialless` is safer for apps that load any cross-origin resources.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -sI https://host/ | grep -i cross-origin-embedder` returns desired value

title: Base compose missing `version:` directive while production.yml:5 still has `version: '3.8'`
description: Inconsistent: base file omits version key (modern Compose Spec), but production/test/ml-production overlays declare `version: '3.8'` (legacy). Mixing causes deprecation warnings and may load different schemas.
recommendation: Either remove `version:` from all compose files (modern) or set consistently. Modern Docker Compose (>=2.0) ignores it but warns.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.production.yml config 2>&1 | grep -i 'version is obsolete'` returns 0

title: nginx service in base compose duplicates production nginx
description: Base `docker-compose.yml` defines an nginx reverse proxy at port 80/443 mounting `infrastructure/docker/nginx/nginx.conf`. Production overlay defines another nginx (line 274) mounting `infrastructure/docker/frontend/nginx.optimized.conf`. Two nginx configs, two paths, hard to reason about.
recommendation: Delete nginx from base compose; let dev use frontend container's embedded nginx. Production overlay owns the load balancer.
acceptance_test_hint: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml config | grep -c 'image: nginx'` is 0 in dev, 1 in prod

title: dev frontend env points to `localhost:8000` but maps port 3000
description: `VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:8000` is a build-time arg in the production Dockerfile but a runtime env in dev compose. Vite only reads `VITE_*` at build time; setting at runtime in dev (line 139) has no effect on a built bundle. Works only because dev compose runs `npm start` (Vite dev server) which does pick up env. Confusing for prod — but in production.yml it is correctly passed as `args:`.
recommendation: Document or move VITE_* into `args` for any built target; clarify in compose comments which mode each block targets.
acceptance_test_hint: comment block at top of docker-compose.yml lists VITE behavior

title: Hard-coded `python3.12` site-packages path
description: `PYTHONPATH=/app:/home/appuser/.local/lib/python3.12/site-packages` — coupled to PYTHON_VERSION ARG (3.12). If ARG changes, path drifts silently.
recommendation: Use `python -c "import site; print(site.USER_SITE)"` at build time, or rely on PATH+sys.path defaults instead of hard-coding.
acceptance_test_hint: bumping PYTHON_VERSION ARG to 3.13 still resolves imports

title: `npm ci --only=production` then trying to run `npm run build`
description: `--only=production` skips devDependencies; Vite, TypeScript, and most build toolchains live in devDependencies. Build typically fails unless those moved to dependencies. infrastructure/docker/frontend/Dockerfile uses `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` (broader).
recommendation: Use `npm ci` (no `--only=production`) in builder stage; production-only install belongs only in serving stage which here is nginx (no Node).
acceptance_test_hint: `docker build -f Dockerfile.frontend .` succeeds without missing-vite errors

title: Script injection via untrusted issue title/body
description: `TITLE="${{ github.event.issue.title }}"` and `BODY="${{ github.event.issue.body }}"` inlined into shell on a `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` job. An attacker filing an issue with a backtick/`$()` payload in the title can execute arbitrary code in CI with the workflow token.
recommendation: Pass user-controlled fields via `env:` and reference as `"$TITLE"` inside `run:`; never interpolate `${{ github.event.* }}` directly into shell.
acceptance_test_hint: Re-run workflow against a test issue with title `$(echo PWNED)`; verify literal string is logged, not command output.

title: Same script-injection pattern in 3 more workflows
description: `PR_BODY="${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}"`, `BODY="${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}"`, and `ISSUE_TITLE/ISSUE_BODY` env values built from raw event fields. Same RCE-in-CI risk as F-14-001.
recommendation: Apply same env-var-then-quote remediation. Audit all 30 workflows for `${{ github.event.*.title
acceptance_test_hint: body | message }}` inside `run:` blocks. | `grep -nE "(TITLE | BODY | MESSAGE | NAME)=\"\\\$\{\{ *github\\.event" .github/workflows/*.yml` returns 0.

file_line: .github/workflows/ci.yml:278; comprehensive-testing.yml:34,88,179,292; daily-pipeline-validation.yml; dependency-updates.yml; production-deploy.yml; reusable-test.yml; security-scan.yml
title: TA-Lib downloaded over plaintext HTTP without checksum
description: `wget http://prdownloads.sourceforge.net/ta-lib/ta-lib-0.4.0-src.tar.gz` runs in 7+ workflows. No HTTPS, no SHA256 verification → trivially MITM'd by any on-path attacker (CI runners egress through public internet). The unpacked source is then `make install`'d as root.
recommendation: Switch to HTTPS, pin to known SHA256, OR build TA-Lib once into a base Docker image consumed via `container:`.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -E "wget http://prdownloads" .github/workflows/*.yml` returns 0; new install step has `sha256sum -c`.

title: Third-party actions pinned only to floating major tags
description: `uses: docker/build-push-action@v5`, `8398a7/action-slack@v3`, `dawidd6/action-send-mail@v3`, `appleboy/ssh-action@v1`, `gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v2`, `returntocorp/semgrep-action@v1`, `anchore/sbom-action@v0`, `hadolint/hadolint-action@v3`, etc. — `grep -E "uses:.*@[a-f0-9]{40}"` returns 0 hits. A compromised tag (Tj-actions style supply-chain attack) executes immediately on next CI run.
recommendation: Pin every third-party action to a full 40-char commit SHA with a comment indicating the tag, e.g. `uses: docker/build-push-action@4f580a... # v5.3.0`. Configure Dependabot ecosystem `github-actions` (already on per `.github/dependabot.yml:115`) to bump SHAs.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -cE "uses: [^@]+@[a-f0-9]{40}" .github/workflows/*.yml` ≥ count of `uses:` lines for non-`actions/*` and non-`./` references.

title: Two duplicate mypy workflows with conflicting configs
description: `mypy.yml` runs Python 3.11; `type-check.yml` runs Python 3.12, has a 3636-error baseline gate. Triggers overlap (both fire on `backend/**/*.py` PRs to main/develop). Wastes runner minutes and produces conflicting status checks.
recommendation: Keep `type-check.yml` (newer, has baseline gate); delete `mypy.yml`. Or merge into a single workflow with matrix.
acceptance_test_hint: After consolidation, `ls .github/workflows/{mypy,type-check}.yml` shows only one; PR builds run mypy exactly once.

file_line: .github/workflows/cleanup.yml; documentation-sync.yml; daily-pipeline-validation.yml; comprehensive-testing.yml; migration-check.yml; automated-release.yml; mypy.yml; dependency-updates.yml; performance-monitoring.yml; reusable-build.yml; pr-automation.yml; monitoring-notifications.yml
title: Workflows missing top-level `permissions:` block
description: `grep -c "permissions:" .github/workflows/*.yml` shows 0 for these workflows, so they inherit the repo default (often `contents: write` for legacy repos). Violates least-privilege; if a step is compromised it gets write access to repo contents and packages.
recommendation: Add `permissions: contents: read` (or narrower) at workflow top; grant write only on the specific job that needs it.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -L "^permissions:" .github/workflows/*.yml` returns empty (every workflow declares permissions).

title: Mixed CodeQL action versions (`@v2` and `@v3`)
description: `grep github/codeql-action .github/workflows/*.yml` shows `init@v3`, `analyze@v3`, but `upload-sarif@v2` co-exists with `upload-sarif@v3`. v2 is deprecated by GitHub and will be removed; mismatched versions can drop SARIF uploads silently.
recommendation: Standardize on `github/codeql-action/*@v3` everywhere.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep "codeql-action.*@v2" .github/workflows/*.yml` returns 0.

title: Python matrix wastes ~3x compute (3.10/3.11/3.12) for a single deployment target
description: Backend ships on Python 3.12 only (`PYTHON_VERSION: '3.12'` env, Dockerfile.backend uses 3.12). Matrix tests on 3.10 and 3.11 burn CI minutes for versions that never run in prod and have already produced failures (3.9 was dropped per inline comment).
recommendation: Reduce matrix to `['3.12']` OR justify with explicit "library-style" reasoning. Move 3.10/3.11 to a nightly-only job.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep "python-version: \[" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns single-element list.

title: `reusable-build.yml` is never called
description: `grep -rn "uses:.*reusable-build" .github/workflows/` returns 0 hits. The 7,202-byte reusable workflow is dead code. `reusable-test.yml` IS called (by `workflow-coordinator.yml:142`) — so this is selective dead code, not a global pattern.
recommendation: Either wire `workflow-coordinator.yml` build job to call `reusable-build.yml`, or delete the file.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "uses: ./.github/workflows/reusable-build" .github/` returns ≥1 OR the file no longer exists.

title: `codecov/codecov-action@v4` requires `CODECOV_TOKEN` for private repos but `fail_ci_if_error: false` masks misconfiguration
description: Two upload steps reference `secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN`. If unset on a fork or new repo, uploads silently fail because `fail_ci_if_error: false`. Coverage gates downstream become meaningless.
recommendation: Add a smoke-check step that warns when `CODECOV_TOKEN == ''`; or set `fail_ci_if_error: ${{ github.repository_owner == 'devinmcgrath' }}`.
acceptance_test_hint: A test PR with `CODECOV_TOKEN` unset emits a `::warning::` annotation.

title: Many backend-quality steps swallow exit codes with `\
recommendation: true`
acceptance_test_hint: `safety check ... \ | \ | true`, `bandit ... \ | \ | true`, `pip-audit ... \ | \ | true`, `mypy ... \ | \ | true` make the step always green even when issues are found. Reports are uploaded as artifacts but no gate exists in `backend-quality`. (Note: `backend-security` job at line 145+ does parse and gate — that's the correct pattern.) | Mirror the parsing-and-gate pattern from `backend-security`; or remove duplicated checks from `backend-quality` since they're authoritatively run elsewhere. | `grep -nE "(bandit\ | safety\ | pip-audit\ | mypy).*\\ | \\ | true" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns 0 OR each is followed by an explicit parse step.

title: `additional_dependencies: [types-all]` is unmaintained
description: `types-all` (PyPI) was deprecated in 2022 and is a meta-package that often fails to resolve. Pre-commit silently caches the failure on first run.
recommendation: Replace with explicit type stubs actually needed: `[types-python-dateutil, types-requests, types-PyYAML, lxml]` matching `type-check.yml:34`.
acceptance_test_hint: `pre-commit run --all-files mypy` succeeds in a clean cache.

description: `path: /var/cache/apt` requires sudo to read; cache hits fail silently. Adds runtime without benefit.
recommendation: Either remove the apt cache step, or migrate to `awalsh128/cache-apt-pkgs-action` (community) pinned by SHA.
